p.i: An account of Alma and the Lord’s people, who were driven into the wilderness by king Noah’s people.

chapter.li: LEChapter23 Verse1 The Lord warned Alma that king Noah’s armies were coming to attack them, and Alma told his people. So they gathered their flocks, took their grain, and went into the wilderness ahead of king Noah’s armies. VerseEnd Verse2 The Lord gave them strength, so they stayed ahead of king Noah’s people coming to kill them. VerseEnd Verse3 They fled into the wilderness for eight days, VerseEnd Verse4 arriving at a very beautiful and pleasant land with fresh water. VerseEnd Verse5 They pitched their tents there and began to farm the ground and construct buildings, etc. - 2PP you see, they were productive and hard working. VerseEnd

Verse6 And the people wanted Alma to be their king, since they loved and trusted him. VerseEnd Verse7 But he told them: It isn’t advisable for us to have a king. This is what the Lord has said: 2PP You must not value one person over another, and no one should consider themselves better than another. Therefore I advise 2PP you against having a king. VerseEnd Verse8 However, if it were possible to always have ethical men as 2PP your kings, it would be worthwhile to have a king — VerseEnd Verse9 but remember the iniquity of king Noah and his priests. I was trapped in it and did many wicked things offensive to the Lord, that I now bitterly regret. VerseEnd Verse10 But after a lot of suffering, the Lord heard and answered my prayers and has turned me into an instrument in His hands to teach many of 2PP you knowledge about His truth. VerseEnd Verse11 Nevertheless, I don’t expect praise for this, since I’m unworthy of taking any pride in myself. VerseEnd Verse12 Now I tell 2PP you: King Noah oppressed 2PP you, and he and his priests enslaved 2PP you and led 2PP you into iniquity, so 2PP you were captured with the chains of sin. VerseEnd Verse13 Now as God’s power has freed 2PP you from these chains, from the control of king Noah and his people, and from the chains of sin, I want 2PP you to maintain 2PP your liberty, and never trust any man to be a king ruling 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse14 Don’t trust anyone to be 2PP your teacher or minister unless he’s called by God, walking in His ways, and following His commandments. VerseEnd Verse15 This is what Alma taught his people, that everyone should love their neighbor as themselves, and they shouldn’t have any serious conflicts. VerseEnd

Verse16 Now Alma, their congregation’s founder, was their high priest. VerseEnd Verse17 And no one received authority to preach or teach unless it was from God and through Alma. He alone ordained all their priests and teachers, and no one was ordained unless they were ethical men. VerseEnd Verse18 So they cared for their people and taught them things required for righteousness. VerseEnd Verse19 And they began to thrive in the land, which they called Helam. VerseEnd Verse20 They increased in numbers and produced more than they needed in the land of Helam. They built a city that they called the city of Helam. VerseEnd Verse21 However, the Lord disciplines His people; He requires them to be patient and faithful. VerseEnd Verse22 Nevertheless, whoever trusts Him will be rewarded on the last day; and this is how it was with Alma’s people. VerseEnd Verse23 I’ll show 2PP you that they were subjected to slavery, and no one could have freed them other than the Lord who is God: the God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob. VerseEnd Verse24 He freed them and demonstrated His mighty power to them, making them rejoice. VerseEnd

Verse25 What happened was that while they were in the land of Helam, in the city of Helam, while farming the surrounding land, a Lamanite army came into the outskirts of the land. VerseEnd Verse26 And Alma’s people ran from their fields and gathered in the city of Helam, being very frightened at the Lamanites’ arrival. VerseEnd Verse27 But Alma went out and joined with them and urged them to not be frightened, but to remember the Lord their God, that He would protect them. VerseEnd Verse28 So they subdued their fears and began to pray to the Lord to soften the Lamanites’ hearts so they would spare them and their wives and children. VerseEnd Verse29 And the Lord softened the Lamanites’ hearts. Alma and his people went out and surrendered to them, and the Lamanites took control of Helam. VerseEnd

Verse30 Now the Lamanite armies, who had gone in pursuit of king Limhi’s people, had been lost in the wilderness for many days. VerseEnd Verse31 But they had found those priests of king Noah in a place they called Amulon, where they had settled and farmed. VerseEnd Verse32 Now the name of the leader of those priests was Amulon. VerseEnd Verse33 And Amulon pled with the Lamanites and sent out their wives, who were the Lamanites’ daughters, to plead with their relatives not to kill their husbands. VerseEnd Verse34 And the Lamanites had sympathy for Amulon and his men and didn’t kill them because of their wives. VerseEnd Verse35 So Amulon and his men joined the Lamanites, and they were traveling in the wilderness in search of the land of Nephi when they discovered the land of Helam, where Alma and his people had settled. VerseEnd

Verse36 The Lamanites promised Alma and his people that if they would show them the way to the land of Nephi they would spare their lives and respect their liberty. VerseEnd Verse37 But after Alma had shown them the way leading to the land of Nephi, the Lamanites refused to keep their promise, and instead set guards over Alma and his people, surrounding the land of Helam. VerseEnd Verse38 And the rest of them went to the land of Nephi; and some of those returned to Helam, bringing with them the wives and children of the guards who had been left behind. VerseEnd Verse39 The king of the Lamanites appointed Amulon to be a king and ruler over his people in Helam. However, he was only given power to obey the will of the king of the Lamanites. VerseEnd

LEChapter24 Verse1 And Amulon earned the trust of the king of the Lamanites, so the king allowed him and his men to be appointed teachers of his people in the lands of Shemlon, Shilom, and Amulon. VerseEnd Verse2 The Lamanites had control of all these lands; so the king of the Lamanites had appointed rulers over each of them. VerseEnd Verse3 Now the name of the king of the Lamanites was Laman, and he was named after his father, and was called king Laman. He ruled over many people. VerseEnd Verse4 He appointed teachers from Amulon’s men in every land occupied by his people. So the Nephite language began to be taught to all the Lamanites. VerseEnd Verse5 And they were people that were friendly with each other. Nevertheless, they didn’t know about God, and Amulon’s men didn’t teach them anything about the Lord God, the Law of Moses, or Abinadi’s words. VerseEnd Verse6 But they taught them to write a record, enabling them to write to each other as well. VerseEnd Verse7 So the Lamanites became wealthier and began to trade with each other and grow strong and become shrewd and sly, like worldly men are — indeed, very sly, enjoying all kinds of wickedness and plunder, but they didn’t cheat their own people. VerseEnd

Verse8 Now Amulon began to abuse Alma and his people and persecute him and have his children mistreat and harass their children. VerseEnd Verse9 This was because Amulon recognized Alma had been one of the king’s priests and was the one who believed Abinadi’s words and was thrown out by the king. So he was very angry with him. Although he had to obey king Laman, Amulon still abused Alma’s people, demanding work from them and putting taskmasters over them. VerseEnd Verse10 Their afflictions were so intense that they began to pray constantly to God. VerseEnd Verse11 Amulon ordered them to stop praying and put guards over them to watch them, to execute whoever was found calling upon God. VerseEnd Verse12 So Alma and his people didn’t pray out loud to the Lord their God but instead poured out their hearts to Him, and He understood the thoughts of their hearts. VerseEnd

Verse13 And the Lord’s voice came to them as they suffered, saying: Lift up 2PP your heads and be of good cheer. I’m aware of the covenant 2PP you made with Me. And I promise this people of Mine that I’ll free 2PP you from slavery. VerseEnd Verse14 I’ll also ease the burdens put upon 2PP your shoulders, so that 2PP you can’t feel them on 2PP your backs, for as long as 2PP you remain in slavery. I’ll do this so 2PP you can stand as witnesses for Me after this, and know for certain that I the Lord God am with My people as they suffer. VerseEnd Verse15 Now the burdens placed on Alma and his people were made light — the Lord gave them the strength to carry them with ease — and they submitted cheerfully and patiently to the Lord’s will. VerseEnd

Verse16 Their faith and patience were so great that the Lord’s voice spoke again, saying: Be of good cheer, because I’ll free 2PP you from slavery tomorrow. VerseEnd Verse17 He told Alma: 2PSI You will lead this people, and I’ll go with 2PSI you and free them from slavery. VerseEnd

Verse18 Now Alma and his people gathered their flocks and grain at night — indeed, they spent the whole night herding their flocks. VerseEnd Verse19 And in the morning, the Lord caused a deep sleep to overcome the Lamanites, and all their taskmasters were sound asleep. VerseEnd Verse20 Then Alma and his people made their way into the wilderness. And when they had traveled all day, they pitched their tents in a valley, calling it Alma, because he led their way in the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse21 They poured out their thanks to God in the valley of Alma because He had been merciful to them and eased their burdens and freed them from slavery — and no one could have set them free from their enslavement except for the Lord who is God. VerseEnd Verse22 And they gave thanks to God — indeed, all the men, women, and children who could speak raised their voices, giving praise to God. VerseEnd

Verse23 Now the Lord told Alma: Act quickly and get yourself and these people out of this land. The Lamanites have reawakened and are pursuing 2PSI you. So get out of this land, and I’ll stop the Lamanites in this valley, so they don’t come any further in pursuit of this people. VerseEnd Verse24 And they left the valley and traveled into the wilderness. VerseEnd Verse25 After they had been in the wilderness for twelve days, they arrived in Zarahemla, and king Mosiah also received them joyfully. VerseEnd

LEChapter25 Verse1 Now king Mosiah called all the people together. VerseEnd Verse2 This included the people of Zarahemla who were descendants of Muloch and those who came with him into the wilderness, who outnumbered the children of Nephi or the descendants of Nephi. VerseEnd Verse3 But the Lamanites outnumbered the Nephites and Zarahemla’s people by more than two to one. VerseEnd Verse4 Now all the Nephites and Zarahemla’s people gathered, and they were divided into two groups. VerseEnd

Verse5 Then Mosiah reviewed Zeniff’s records and had them read to his people. Those records covered Zeniff’s people from the time they left Zarahemla until they returned. VerseEnd Verse6 He also read the account of Alma and his people and all their difficulties, from the time they left Zarahemla until they returned. VerseEnd Verse7 When Mosiah had finished reading the records, the people who had remained in the land were shocked and amazed — VerseEnd Verse8 they didn’t know what to think. When they saw those who had been freed from slavery, they were filled with overwhelming joy. VerseEnd Verse9 But when they thought of their relatives who had been killed by the Lamanites, they mourned and shed many tears. VerseEnd Verse10 When they thought of God’s immediate goodness and His power in freeing Alma and his people from the Lamanites and from slavery, they sang and gave thanks to God. VerseEnd Verse11 But when they thought of the Lamanites, their relatives, of their sinful, polluted state, they were filled with pain and sorrow for their souls’ well-being. VerseEnd

Verse12 And the children of Amulon and his men, who had married the Lamanite young women, were embarrassed at their fathers’ conduct and didn’t want to be associated with their fathers’ name. So they changed their name to Nephi, so they could be called Nephi’s children and be included with those who were called Nephites. VerseEnd Verse13 All of Zarahemla’s people were included as Nephites, because Nephi’s descendants governed the kingdom. VerseEnd

Verse14 When Mosiah finished reading these records to the people, he wanted Alma to also speak to them. VerseEnd Verse15 So Alma spoke to them as they were gathered in large groups, going from one group to another, preaching repentance and faith in the Lord to the people. VerseEnd Verse16 And he urged Limhi’s people and everyone who had been freed from slavery to remember it was the Lord who had rescued them. VerseEnd Verse17 After Alma finished teaching the people many things and concluded his preaching, king Limhi wanted to be baptized and so did all his people. VerseEnd Verse18 Therefore Alma went into the water and baptized them in the very same way he baptized his people in the waters of Mormon. And all those he baptized belonged to God’s congregation — because of their belief in Alma’s words. VerseEnd

Verse19 Then king Mosiah authorized Alma to organize congregations throughout the land of Zarahemla, letting him ordain priests and teachers over each one. VerseEnd Verse20 Now they did this because there were too many people for only one teacher to guide them, or to be able to hear God’s word in one group. VerseEnd Verse21 So they gathered in different groups called congregations, every congregation having priests and teachers, and every priest’s messages repeating Alma’s instruction. VerseEnd Verse22 And so, even though there were many congregations, they were all one congregation: God’s congregation; because nothing was preached in any of the congregations except for repentance and faith in God. VerseEnd Verse23 Now there were seven congregations in the land of Zarahemla. And whoever wanted to take upon himself the name of Christ, or of God, joined the congregations of God; VerseEnd Verse24 and they were called God’s people. The Lord poured out His Spirit upon them, and they were blessed and prospered in the land. VerseEnd

LEChapter26 Verse1 But many of the younger generation couldn’t understand king Benjamin’s words since they were little children when he addressed his people. They didn’t believe their ancestors’ traditions. VerseEnd Verse2 They didn’t believe what had been said about the resurrection of the dead nor did they believe in Christ’s coming. VerseEnd Verse3 Now because of their unbelief, they didn’t accept God’s word. And their hearts were hardened, VerseEnd Verse4 and they refused to be baptized or join the congregation. They were a separate people concerning their faith and remained separated from then on, staying in their carnal and sinful state because they wouldn’t call on the Lord their God. VerseEnd Verse5 Now during Mosiah’s rule they weren’t half as numerous as God’s people, but because of divisions in the congregation, they grew in numbers. VerseEnd Verse6 They misled many in the congregation with their persuasive words and led them to commit many sins. As a result, the congregation needed to admonish their members who committed sins. VerseEnd

Verse7 So the teachers took the offenders to the priests; and the priests took them to Alma, the high priest. VerseEnd Verse8 King Mosiah gave Alma control over the congregation, VerseEnd Verse9 and Alma was aware of these offenders because there were many witnesses against them — indeed, many people came forward and testified of their iniquity. VerseEnd Verse10 Now nothing like this had happened before in the congregation, so Alma was deeply troubled and he took them to the king. VerseEnd Verse11 He said to the king: We’ve brought to 2PSI you those who have been accused by their associates. They’ve been found committing various iniquities and won’t repent of their iniquities. So we bring them to 2PSI you, so 2PSI you can judge them based on their crimes. VerseEnd Verse12 But king Mosiah told Alma: I’m not going to judge them. Therefore I give them back to 2PSI you to be judged. VerseEnd Verse13 Now Alma was deeply troubled again. So he went and asked the Lord what to do about the problem, since he was afraid to do wrong in God’s sight. VerseEnd

Verse14 After he had poured out his whole soul to God, the Lord’s voice spoke to him, saying: VerseEnd Verse15 2PSI You are blessed, Alma. And those who were baptized in the waters of Mormon are blessed also. 2PSI You are blessed because of 2PSI your great faith based upon My servant Abinadi’s words. VerseEnd Verse16 And they’re blessed because of their great faith based upon the words 2PSI you’ve taught them. VerseEnd Verse17 And 2PSI you are blessed because 2PSI you’ve established a congregation among this people. They will be strengthened and be My people. VerseEnd Verse18 And this people is blessed, those who are willing to bear My name; they’ll be called in My name, and they’re Mine. VerseEnd Verse19 Because 2PSI you’ve asked Me about those who have done wrong, 2PSI you are blessed. VerseEnd Verse20 2PSI You are My servant, and I covenant with 2PSI you that 2PSI you will have eternal life.

2PSI You will serve Me, go out in My name, and gather My sheep. VerseEnd Verse21 And any who hear My voice will be My sheep; and 2PP you will receive them into the congregation, and I’ll also receive them. VerseEnd Verse22 This is My congregation. Whoever is baptized will be baptized as a sign of repentance; and whoever 2PP you receive must believe in My name, and I’ll freely forgive them. VerseEnd Verse23 I Am the one who takes upon Myself the sins of the world, since I Am the one who created them. I Am the one who, in the end, will give to those who believe a place at My right hand. VerseEnd Verse24 They’re called in My name; and if they know Me, they’ll come forward and have a place eternally at My right hand. VerseEnd Verse25 And when the second trumpet sounds, those who never knew Me will arise and stand in front of Me. VerseEnd Verse26 And then they’ll know that I Am the Lord their God, that I am their Redeemer, but they won’t be redeemed. VerseEnd Verse27 Then I’ll declare to them that I never knew them, and they’ll go away into everlasting fire prepared for the accuser and his angels. VerseEnd Verse28 Therefore I tell 2PP you that 2PP you must not receive into My congregation any who refuse to hear My voice, because I won’t welcome them on the last day. VerseEnd

Verse29 Therefore I tell 2PP you: Go; 2PP you must judge whoever sins against Me according to the sins they’ve committed. And if a person confesses their sins before 2PSI you and Me and repents in the sincerity of their heart, 2PP you must forgive them; and I’ll forgive them also. VerseEnd Verse30 And as often as My people repent I’ll forgive them of their offenses against Me. VerseEnd Verse31 And 2PP you must also forgive each other’s offenses. I tell 2PP you truthfully: The person who doesn’t forgive their neighbor’s offenses when they say they repent, that person brings themselves under condemnation. VerseEnd Verse32 Now I tell 2PP you: Go; and whoever won’t repent of their sins, the same won’t be included among My people. And this shall be observed from now on. VerseEnd

Verse33 When Alma had heard these words, he wrote them down so he could preserve them and so he could judge the people of the congregation according to God’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse34 And Alma went and judged those who had been caught in iniquity, according to the Lord’s word. VerseEnd Verse35 Whoever repented of their sins and confessed them he counted among the congregation members. VerseEnd Verse36 But those who wouldn’t confess their sins and repent of their iniquity, the same weren’t included among the congregation members and their names were erased. VerseEnd Verse37 So Alma regulated the congregation’s business. And they again began to have peace and abundance in the congregation, walking mindfully before God, receiving and baptizing many. VerseEnd Verse38 Now Alma and his fellow laborers who led the congregation did all these things, being very diligent, carefully teaching God’s word, yet encountering many challenges, and being persecuted by those who didn’t belong to God’s congregation. VerseEnd Verse39 They admonished their brothers and sisters and each one was also admonished by God’s word if they had erred or had sinned, being commanded by God to pray always and to give thanks in all things. VerseEnd LEChapter27 Verse1 Now the unbelievers mistreated and harassed those of the congregation so much that they began to grumble and complain to their leaders about it, and they complained to Alma. And Alma brought the case before their king, Mosiah, who consulted with his counselors. VerseEnd

Verse2 King Mosiah sent a proclamation throughout the land that no unbeliever should mistreat or hurt anyone who belonged to God’s congregation. VerseEnd Verse3 And a strict command went among all the congregations that there must not be any persecution among them, but there should be equality among all of them, VerseEnd Verse4 that they shouldn’t let any pride or arrogance disrupt the peace, everyone should value their neighbor as themselves and work with their own hands to support themselves, VerseEnd Verse5 and their priests and teachers should work with their own hands for their support in every case except for sickness or extreme poverty. As they did these things, they abounded in God’s grace. VerseEnd Verse6 And great peace began to prevail once more in the land. The people grew very numerous and began to spread out over the land — to the north, south, east, and west — building large cities and villages in every quarter of the land. VerseEnd Verse7 And the Lord blessed them and caused them to prosper, and they increased in number and became wealthy. VerseEnd

Verse8 Now Mosiah’s sons were included among the unbelievers, and so was one of Alma’s sons, who was named Alma after his father. Nevertheless, he had become a very wicked man who worshiped idols, and he was eloquent and charmed the people with his persuasive language. Therefore he led many of them to follow him into sinning against God. VerseEnd Verse9 And he interfered with the prosperity of God’s congregation, stealing away people’s hearts, causing many strong disagreements among them, and giving God’s enemy the opportunity to influence them. VerseEnd

Verse10 While he was out trying to destroy God’s congregation (doing it secretly with Mosiah’s sons), trying to destroy the congregation and lead the Lord’s people astray, violating not only God’s commandments but also the king’s — VerseEnd Verse11 and as I told 2PP you, as they were going about rebelling against God, the angel of the Lord appeared to them, descending in what seemed like a cloud. He spoke with a voice like thunder, making the ground shake where they were standing. VerseEnd Verse12 Their astonishment was so great that they fell to the ground and didn’t understand the words he spoke. VerseEnd Verse13 But he called out again, saying: Alma, get up and step forward. Why do 2PSI you persecute God’s congregation? Because the Lord has said: This is My congregation and I’ll establish it, and nothing will destroy it except for My people’s transgressions. VerseEnd Verse14 The angel also said: The Lord has heard His people’s prayers and the prayers of His servant Alma, 2PSI your father. He’s prayed with great faith about 2PSI you, so 2PSI you could be brought to the knowledge of the truth. Therefore I’ve come to convince 2PSI you of God’s power and authority, so His servants’ prayers will be answered according to their faith. VerseEnd Verse15 Can 2PSF you challenge God’s power? Does my voice not shake the earth? Can 2PSF you not see me in front of 2PSF you? I am sent from God. VerseEnd Verse16 Now I tell 2PSI you: Go; and remember the slavery of 2PSI your people in the lands of Helam and Nephi, and remember how He has done great things for them. They were enslaved and He set them free. Now I tell 2PSI you, Alma: Go 2PSI your way, and so that their prayers will be answered, end 2PSI your efforts to destroy the congregation, unless 2PSI you want to be destroyed! VerseEnd Verse17 Now these were the last words the angel said to Alma, as he left. VerseEnd

Verse18 Now Alma and those who were with him fell down on the ground again, since they were so astonished, having seen an angel of the Lord with their own eyes, and his voice was like thunder that shook the ground. They knew there was nothing except for God’s power that could shake the ground and make it tremble as if it would split apart. VerseEnd Verse19 Alma was so dumbfounded that he couldn’t talk or open his mouth. And he was weak and couldn’t even move his hands. So those who were with him took him and carried him in a helpless condition, putting him down in front of his father. VerseEnd Verse20 They told his father all that had happened to them. And he was glad, because he knew that it was God’s power. VerseEnd Verse21 And he had many people gather so they could witness what the Lord had done for his son and for those who were with him. VerseEnd Verse22 And he had the priests assemble and they began to fast and pray to the Lord their God that He would open Alma’s mouth so he could speak, so his limbs could receive their strength, and so the people’s eyes could be opened, to see and know about God’s goodness and glory. VerseEnd

Verse23 After they had fasted and prayed for two days and nights, Alma’s arms and legs had their strength return. And he stood up and began to speak to them, telling them to be of good cheer. VerseEnd Verse24 He said: I’ve repented of my sins and have been redeemed by the Lord. I’m born of the Spirit. VerseEnd Verse25 And the Lord said to me: Don’t be surprised that all mankind, men and women — people of every nation, tribe, and language — must be born again, born of God, changed from their carnal and fallen state to a state of righteousness, being redeemed by God, becoming His sons and daughters. VerseEnd Verse26 Therefore they become new creatures. And unless they do this, there’s no way for them to inherit God’s kingdom. VerseEnd Verse27 I tell 2PP you: If they don’t follow God, they’ll be rejected. I know this because I was on the verge of being rejected. VerseEnd Verse28 Nevertheless, after wading through great distress, repenting close to death, the Lord, in His mercy, has seen fit to rescue me suddenly from an everlasting burning; and I’m born of God. VerseEnd Verse29 My soul has been redeemed from a state of suffering in bondage of sin. I was in the darkest abyss, but now I see God’s marvelous light. My soul was tortured with eternal torment, but I was quickly rescued, and my soul isn’t pained anymore. VerseEnd Verse30 I rejected my Redeemer and denied what our fathers had said. But now I know that they correctly predicted He will come, and that He remembers every creature of His creation, and He will reveal Himself to everyone. VerseEnd Verse31 Every knee will bow and every tongue will acknowledge Him in His presence. They’ll acknowledge He is God on the last day, when all mankind stands to be judged by Him. Then those who live on earth without God will acknowledge that the judgment they receive of everlasting punishment is right and fair. They’ll shake, tremble, and recoil at a glance from His all-searching eye. VerseEnd

Verse32 Now Alma and those who were with him when the angel appeared to them began to teach the people from then on, traveling throughout the land, declaring to the people what they had heard and seen, preaching God’s word in very trying circumstances: receiving very harsh treatment by unbelievers and getting beaten by many of them. VerseEnd Verse33 But despite all this, they imparted great comfort to the congregation, confirming their faith and urging them with long-suffering and consistent effort to keep God’s commandments. VerseEnd Verse34 Four of them were Mosiah’s sons: Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni; these were the names of Mosiah’s sons. VerseEnd Verse35 They traveled throughout the land of Zarahemla and among all the people who were under king Mosiah’s rule, earnestly trying to repair all the harm they had done to the congregation, confessing their sins, explaining everything they had seen, and teaching the prophecies and scriptures to all who wanted to hear them. VerseEnd Verse36 So they were instruments in God’s hands in bringing many to know the truth and their Redeemer. VerseEnd Verse37 And how blessed are they! Because they proclaimed peace and good news of good things, declaring to the people that the Lord reigns. VerseEnd
